parole.significato: a type of trap, used to catch birds or other small animals
parole.testo: Borrowed from Língua Geral Amazônica gûyrapuka (“bird trap”).
Borrowed from Língua Geral Amazônica *ûasaku. First attested in 1763.

parole.significato: a dish of northern Brazil made with paracress (jambu), tucupi, tapioca starch, and dried shrimps.
parole.testo: Uncertain, though possibly borrowed from Língua Geral Amazônica takaká, of unknown origin.

parole.significato: tucupi (yellow sauce made from wild manioc root)
parole.testo: Borrowed from Língua Geral Amazônica tykupy, possibly from Old Tupi tyku (“liquid”) + upir (“to rise”), literally “the liquid that rises”, as tucupi is prepared from the liquid portion of the manioc juice, separated from the manioc solids by decanting.
